question: PGA Tour pros face two putts of equal length, one for birdie and one for par. Which do they hole more often?
answer: The par putt. Pope and Schweitzer analysed millions of laser-measured putts and found par putts holed a few percentage points more often than birdie putts from the same distance. Missing par feels like losing a stroke; missing birdie, like failing to gain one. So birdie putts are struck more timidly and stop short.
move: A loss looms larger than an equal gain, so check your caution.
ask: Am I playing safer when chasing a gain than when avoiding a loss of the same size?
trap: Assuming top professionals putt the same whatever the score.
reference: Devin G. Pope & Maurice E. Schweitzer, Is Tiger Woods Loss Averse? Persistent Bias in the Face of Experience, Competition, and High Stakes, American Economic Review, 2011
